title: European versus American audiences
summary: He talks to audiences, and tells jokes about Wales and Slough.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Is there much difference between audiences in Europe and in the United States?

No. You wouldn't believe...I'll tell you this, Dan, I talk when I play. I talk to the audience. And do you know that most of the times they understand me? If I say something funny, they laugh. So evidently they understand me, or somebody next to them will tell them. For example, I was in London and the agent had me going down to Brigdend......that's down in Wales. So I was on the stage, talking, and the promoter said...impresario said, "Well, how do you like Wales?" I says, "Wales, what do you mean, Wales?" I said, "I thought Wales was in Scotland." And everybody fell out. And then another time...I took that and I used to tell it. And the next thing I knew I was in a town called Slough. /Slough, isn't it? You know the term?

Yeah, anyway, I called it...whatever it was, I always intentionally mispronounced it and they cracked up. And whenever I'd say it...'cause "slew" is...was "slough." And they'd all crack up, you know. But audiences are almost the same.
